places.name: Cairo (Downtown / Zamalek)
places.note: Arrival city and base for Giza, Saqqara and the museums.
places.summary: A huge, loud, friendly megacity of 22 million. Downtown around Tahrir Square has the Egyptian Museum and faded belle-époque streets; Zamalek, an island in the Nile, is the leafy, quieter area with cafés and hotels.
facts: Use Uber or Careem: cheap, fixed price, no haggling
Traffic is the real timetable: allow 45–90 min across the city
Metro line 1 and 2 are cheap and quick; women-only carriages exist
places.season: Nov–Dec: 18–24 °C by day, cool evenings. Bring a light jacket.

places.name: Giza (pyramid-view hotels)
places.note: Hotels by the plateau's Sphinx gate: wake up to the pyramids, walk in at opening time.
places.summary: Sleeping by the pyramids (Nazlet el-Semman) saves the morning drive across Cairo and puts the Grand Egyptian Museum 5 minutes away. Rooftop breakfasts look straight at the Sphinx.
facts: Mostly small hotels and guesthouses
Touts are persistent near the gates: a firm 'la, shukran' (no, thanks) works

places.name: Pyramids of Giza & the Sphinx
places.summary: The last standing wonder of the ancient world: the Great Pyramid of Khufu, Khafre's pyramid with its casing cap, Menkaure's, and the Great Sphinx below them. Walk the plateau, then go to the panorama point for the classic all-pyramids view.
facts: Plateau ~700 EGP; inside the Great Pyramid ~1,500 EGP extra (tight, hot, steep)
Go at 07:00: cooler and before the tour buses
Electric buses run between the gates and the panorama point
Camel and horse rides: agree price and duration first, and only with healthy animals
places.season: Shade is scarce: hat, sunscreen and 1–2 L of water each, even in winter.
places.caution: Prices are 2025 foreigner adult prices and rise often: check egymonuments.gov.eg. Card only at the ticket office.

places.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
places.summary: The world's largest archaeological museum, beside the pyramids, fully open since November 2025. The Grand Staircase of colossal statues leads to the main galleries, and the complete Tutankhamun collection (over 5,000 objects) is finally shown together.
facts: ~1,200–1,500 EGP; book a timed ticket online
Allow 3–4 h; the Tutankhamun galleries alone take 1 h
Khufu's 4,500-year-old solar boat has its own hall
Café and restaurant on site, with pyramid views

places.name: Egyptian Museum (Tahrir)
places.summary: The old pink museum on Tahrir Square, crammed with 120,000 objects. Many star pieces have moved to the GEM, but it still has the Narmer Palette, Yuya and Tjuyu's treasures and wonderful dusty corners.
facts: ~550 EGP
Easy to combine with Downtown and the Nile Corniche

places.name: National Museum of Egyptian Civilization
places.summary: Home of the Royal Mummies Hall: Ramesses II, Seti I, Hatshepsut and 17 other pharaohs, shown in a dim, respectful underground gallery. The main hall tells Egypt's story from prehistory to today.
facts: ~500 EGP
On the way between Coptic Cairo and the Citadel

places.name: Khan el-Khalili & al-Muizz Street
places.summary: The medieval heart of Cairo. Al-Muizz Street is a living museum of mosques, madrasas and Mamluk palaces; the Khan el-Khalili bazaar spreads around it. Tea at El Fishawy café, then Bab Zuweila gate's minarets for the view.
facts: Best late afternoon into the evening, when it's lit up and lively
Haggle with a smile; start at a third of the first price
Al-Azhar Park nearby has the best sunset view over the city

places.name: Saladin Citadel & Muhammad Ali Mosque
places.summary: Salah ad-Din's 12th-century hilltop fortress, crowned by the Ottoman-style Alabaster Mosque of Muhammad Ali. The terrace looks over a sea of minarets and, on a clear day, the Giza pyramids.
facts: ~550 EGP
Shoulders and knees covered inside the mosques

places.name: Coptic Cairo
places.summary: Old Cairo's Christian quarter inside the Roman fortress of Babylon: the Hanging Church, the Church of Abu Serga (where the Holy Family is said to have sheltered), the Ben Ezra Synagogue and the excellent Coptic Museum.
facts: Churches free; Coptic Museum ~300 EGP
Mar Girgis metro station is right outside

places.name: Ibn Tulun Mosque & Gayer-Anderson Museum
places.summary: Cairo's oldest intact mosque (879 AD): a vast, calm courtyard with a unique spiral minaret you can climb. The Gayer-Anderson house next door is a beautifully furnished Ottoman mansion.
facts: Mosque free; closed to visitors during Friday midday prayers
Minaret climb gives a great view of the Citadel

places.name: Saqqara (Step Pyramid of Djoser)
places.summary: The necropolis of Memphis and the world's first monumental stone building, Djoser's Step Pyramid (c. 2670 BC). Painted private tombs (Mereruka, Kagemni), the Serapeum's giant bull sarcophagi and the Imhotep Museum.
facts: ~600 EGP main site; the Serapeum and some tombs extra
Far fewer crowds than Giza
Usually done with Dahshur and Memphis as a half-day by driver

places.name: Dahshur (Red & Bent Pyramids)
places.summary: Sneferu's two great pyramids, older than Giza's, in open desert: the Bent Pyramid, whose angle changes halfway up, and the Red Pyramid, the first true smooth-sided pyramid. You can climb down into the Red Pyramid, often alone.
facts: ~200 EGP
The Red Pyramid's passage is 60 m down a low ramp: hot and ammonia-smelling but unforgettable

places.name: Memphis open-air museum
places.summary: All that's left above ground of the ancient capital: a garden museum with a colossal fallen statue of Ramesses II and an alabaster sphinx. A short stop between Saqqara and Dahshur.
facts: ~250 EGP

places.name: Cairo Tower & Zamalek
places.summary: The 187 m lotus-shaped tower on Gezira island, with a 360° view from the pyramids to the Citadel. Best at sunset, then dinner in Zamalek.
facts: ~350 EGP
Felucca rides on the Nile leave from the Corniche nearby (~1 h, agree price per boat)

places.name: Wadi al-Hitan (Valley of the Whales)
places.summary: A UNESCO site in the Fayoum desert where 40-million-year-old fossil skeletons of walking whales lie in the sand, with a small fossil museum. Wild sandstone formations; often combined with the Wadi el-Rayan waterfalls.
facts: Long day trip from Cairo: ~3.5 h each way, last part on a desert track
Go with a tour or a driver with a 4×4
places.caution: Desert track: go with a local driver who knows it.

places.name: Cairo Airport (CAI)
places.note: Domestic flights mostly from Terminal 3 (EgyptAir) or Terminal 2. Airport hotels for an early flight home.
places.summary: Egypt's main airport, 25 km north-east of Downtown. EgyptAir domestic flights to Luxor, Aswan, Hurghada and Sharm el-Sheikh take about an hour.
facts: Visa on arrival at the bank counters before passport control (US$25)
Allow 45–90 min from Downtown or Giza depending on traffic

places.name: Alexandria (Corniche)
places.summary: Alexander the Great's Mediterranean city: a long sweeping Corniche, faded cafés (Trianon, Délices), fresh seafood and a breeze Cairo never gets. Easy as a long day trip by train, nicer with a night.
facts: Train from Cairo Ramses station ~2.5 h
Fish restaurants: you choose the fish, priced by weight
places.season: Mild, sometimes rainy and windy in winter (Nov–Feb).

places.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
places.summary: The striking tilted-disc library that revives the ancient Library of Alexandria, with a vast reading room, antiquities and manuscript museums and a planetarium.
facts: Check opening days before you go: they change around Friday

places.name: Citadel of Qaitbay
places.summary: A 15th-century fortress at the tip of the harbour, built on the foundations of the Pharos lighthouse, one of the Seven Wonders. Waves crash on the walls in winter.

places.name: Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa
places.summary: A 2nd-century Roman-era burial complex cut three levels into the rock, where Egyptian gods wear Roman armour: a strange, wonderful mix of styles.
facts: Combine with Pompey's Pillar, 5 min away

places.name: Pompey's Pillar & the Serapeum
places.summary: A 27 m red granite column raised for Emperor Diocletian, standing on the site of the Serapeum temple, with two sphinxes and underground galleries.

places.name: Montaza Palace gardens
places.summary: The last king's summer palace (outside only) in big seaside gardens with palm-lined paths and a little bay, at the eastern end of the Corniche.

places.name: El Alamein war cemeteries & museum
places.summary: The WWII battlefield of 1942: the Commonwealth War Cemetery with over 7,000 graves, German and Italian memorials, and a military museum.
facts: ~110 km west of Alexandria

places.name: Luxor (East Bank)
places.summary: Ancient Thebes, the greatest open-air museum on earth. The East Bank (the city) has Karnak and Luxor Temple; the West Bank across the Nile has the royal tombs and mortuary temples. Plan 3 days.
facts: From Cairo: 1 h flight, or the overnight Watania sleeper train (~10 h; book ahead)
The public ferry across the Nile costs a few pounds and takes 10 min
Luxor pass: if you'll see most of the West Bank and Karnak, the Luxor Pass (~US$100–200) can save money; bring a passport photo. Check current conditions on egymonuments.gov.eg.
places.season: Nov–Feb is high season: warm days (25–28 °C), cool nights.

places.name: Luxor West Bank (guesthouses)
places.note: Quiet village guesthouses among sugarcane fields; closest base for the tombs and balloon pick-ups.
places.summary: Staying on the West Bank (Al-Gezira, Al-Bairat) means rural calm, rooftop views of the Theban hills and being at the Valley of the Kings for 06:00 opening.

places.name: Karnak Temple
places.summary: The largest religious complex ever built, added to for 2,000 years. The Great Hypostyle Hall's 134 giant papyrus columns, obelisks of Hatshepsut, the sacred lake and the avenue of ram-headed sphinxes.
facts: ~600 EGP; open-air museum extra
Arrive at opening: soft light and almost empty
Sound & light show in the evenings
places.caution: Prices are 2025 foreigner adult prices and rise often: check egymonuments.gov.eg. Card only at the ticket office.

places.name: Luxor Temple
places.summary: Elegant temple in the middle of town, built by Amenhotep III and Ramesses II, with a mosque still perched in its walls. Best at sunset into the evening, when it's floodlit; the Avenue of Sphinxes runs 2.7 km from here to Karnak.
facts: ~500 EGP
Open until late: ideal for the evening of a travel day

places.name: Luxor Museum
places.summary: A small, beautifully lit museum on the Corniche: a cache of perfect statues found under Luxor Temple, Tutankhamun pieces and two royal mummies.
facts: ~400 EGP
Opening hours vary (sometimes a midday break): check locally

places.name: Valley of the Kings
places.summary: The royal burial valley of the New Kingdom: 63 tombs cut into the hills, their walls still bright with paint. The standard ticket covers three of the open tombs; Tutankhamun, Seti I and Ramesses VI need extra tickets.
facts: ~750 EGP for 3 tombs; Tutankhamun ~700, Ramesses VI ~200, Seti I ~2,000 extra
Go at 06:00 opening: the valley is an oven by noon
Phones can take photos (no flash); cameras may need a permit
places.caution: Prices are 2025 foreigner adult prices and rise often: check egymonuments.gov.eg. Card only at the ticket office.

places.name: Temple of Hatshepsut (Deir el-Bahari)
places.summary: The female pharaoh's terraced temple set against sheer limestone cliffs, strikingly modern-looking. Reliefs show her expedition to the land of Punt.
facts: ~440 EGP
A short drive or a 1 h hill path over the ridge from the Valley of the Kings

places.name: Medinet Habu
places.summary: Ramesses III's mortuary temple, the best preserved on the West Bank, with deep-cut, still-coloured reliefs of battles against the Sea Peoples. Many visitors' favourite, and quiet.
facts: ~300 EGP

places.name: Colossi of Memnon
places.summary: Two 18 m seated statues of Amenhotep III, all that stands of his vast temple. Free, by the road, a quick photo stop.

places.name: Valley of the Queens
places.summary: Tombs of royal wives and princes. Nefertari's tomb, the most beautiful painted tomb in Egypt, has its own expensive ticket and a 10-minute visit limit.
facts: ~300 EGP; Nefertari's tomb ~2,000 EGP extra

places.name: Deir el-Medina (workers' village)
places.summary: The village of the craftsmen who built the royal tombs, with their own small, vividly painted family tombs: everyday life rather than pharaohs.
facts: ~240 EGP

places.name: Ramesseum
places.summary: Ramesses II's mortuary temple with the toppled colossus that inspired Shelley's 'Ozymandias'. Atmospheric and usually empty.

places.name: Hot-air balloon over the West Bank
places.note: Pick-up ~04:45 from your hotel; ~45 min flight at sunrise; back ~08:30.
places.summary: Float over the temples, the green Nile valley and the desert hills at sunrise: one of the best things to do in Egypt. Flights depend on the wind.
facts: ~€60–120 per person, book a licensed operator
Includes hotel pick-up and the boat across the Nile
Then straight on to the Valley of the Kings while it's cool
places.caution: Flights are cancelled in wind; book for your first morning in Luxor so you can retry.

places.name: Dendera Temple of Hathor
places.summary: Perhaps Egypt's best-preserved temple, its ceilings freshly cleaned to brilliant blue. Climb to the roof chapels and see the famous Dendera zodiac (a cast; the original is in the Louvre).
facts: ~450 EGP
~75 min north of Luxor; fits on the road day from Luxor to Hurghada via Qena

places.name: Abydos (Temple of Seti I)
places.summary: The temple of Seti I has the finest raised reliefs in Egypt and the Abydos King List of pharaohs. Remote, so usually combined with Dendera on a long day.
facts: ~400 EGP
~3 h north of Luxor

places.name: Luxor Airport (LXR)
places.summary: Small airport 7 km east of town; EgyptAir flies to Cairo several times a day.

places.name: Aswan (Corniche)
places.summary: Egypt's most relaxed city: the Nile narrows between granite boulders and golden dunes, feluccas drift past Elephantine Island, and Nubian culture is everywhere. Base for Philae and Abu Simbel.
facts: Luxor–Aswan: ~3 h by train or road; Nile cruises take 3–4 nights
Old Cataract Hotel terrace for a sunset drink

places.name: Philae Temple
places.summary: The island temple of Isis, moved stone by stone to Agilkia island to save it from the rising lake. You reach it by motorboat; it's one of Egypt's most romantic sights.
facts: ~550 EGP plus the boat (agree a price per boat)

places.name: Abu Simbel temples
places.summary: Ramesses II's colossal rock-cut temples near the Sudanese border, with four 20 m statues of the king at the entrance, rescued from Lake Nasser in the 1960s. Overwhelming in person.
facts: ~750 EGP
3.5 h each way from Aswan by road (tours leave ~04:00) or a short EgyptAir flight
Staying overnight in the village lets you see it empty at dawn

places.name: Nubian village (Gharb Soheil)
places.summary: Colourful painted houses on the West Bank, reached by boat past the cataract islands. Touristy but warm: tea in a Nubian home, henna, local food.
facts: Boat from the Corniche ~1 h each way; agree the boat price for the round trip

places.name: Unfinished Obelisk
places.summary: A 42 m obelisk abandoned in the granite quarry when it cracked: shows exactly how the ancients cut stone.

places.name: Felucca sail at sunset (Aswan)
places.summary: Drift around Elephantine and Kitchener's Island in a traditional sailing boat as the sun sets over the dunes and the Tomb of the Aga Khan.
facts: Agree price per boat per hour on the Corniche

places.name: Temple of Horus at Edfu
places.summary: The most complete temple in Egypt, roof and all: a Ptolemaic temple to the falcon god Horus. A stop between Luxor and Aswan.
facts: ~550 EGP

places.name: Kom Ombo Temple
places.summary: A double temple on a bend of the Nile, dedicated to the crocodile god Sobek and to Horus, with a museum of mummified crocodiles.
facts: ~350 EGP

places.name: Aswan Airport (ASW)
places.summary: 25 km south-west of town; flights to Cairo and Abu Simbel.

places.name: Hurghada (Marina / Sakkala)
places.summary: The Red Sea's biggest resort: long beaches, all-inclusive hotels and dozens of dive and snorkel boats leaving the marina every morning. El Dahar old town has the souk and fish market.
facts: Boat trips leave 08:00–09:00 from the marina
4 h by road to Luxor
places.season: Sea ~24–26 °C in Nov, ~22 °C by late Dec: a 3–5 mm wetsuit helps on longer snorkels.

places.name: El Gouna
places.summary: A planned lagoon town 25 km north of Hurghada: canals, an Italian-style marina, kitesurf beaches and good restaurants. Calmer and smarter than Hurghada.
facts: Kitesurfing centres at Mangroovy beach
Tuk-tuks and a cheap bus loop get you around

places.name: Giftun Islands & Orange Bay (snorkel boat)
places.summary: A full day on a boat from Hurghada to the protected Giftun islands: two or three snorkel stops on coral reefs full of fish, and white sand at Orange Bay or Mahmya.
facts: ~€30–50 with lunch; national park fee extra (~US$5)
Snorkel gear included; bring a rash vest
places.caution: Boats don't sail when the port closes for wind: keep a spare day.

places.name: Desert safari & Bedouin dinner (Hurghada)
places.summary: Quad or jeep into the Eastern Desert mountains behind Hurghada, a camel ride, sunset, dinner in a Bedouin camp and star-gazing.
facts: ~€25–45; afternoon pick-up
Very touristy; the stars are the best bit

places.name: Hurghada Airport (HRG)
places.summary: Busy international airport 5 km south of the centre; flights to Cairo in 1 h.

places.name: Marsa Alam
places.summary: The wilder southern Red Sea: eco-lodges and dive camps along empty coast, with the best shore reefs in Egypt and a chance of dugongs and dolphins.
facts: ~3.5 h south of Hurghada; its own airport (RMF) has mostly European charters

places.name: Abu Dabbab bay (turtles)
places.summary: A sandy bay with seagrass meadows where green turtles graze a few metres from the beach, sometimes a dugong. Easy snorkelling from the shore.
facts: Beach entry fee ~€10–15
Go early, before the day-trip boats

places.name: Wadi el-Gemal & Sharm el-Luli
places.summary: A national park of desert valleys and mangroves; Sharm el-Luli beach has turquoise water like the Maldives and good snorkelling.
facts: National park fee (~US$5)

places.name: Sharm el-Sheikh (Naama Bay)
places.summary: Resort city at the tip of Sinai and one of the world's great dive destinations: Ras Mohammed and the Straits of Tiran are on the doorstep. Naama Bay is the walkable centre of bars and restaurants.
facts: Hotels along the coast have house reefs: snorkel straight from the jetty
~1 h 15 to Dahab
places.season: Sea ~25 °C in Nov, ~23 °C in Dec. Evenings are cool and can be windy.

places.name: Sharm Old Market & Al Sahaba Mosque
places.summary: Sharm el-Maya's old market quarter: spice and souvenir stalls, shisha cafés and the huge, ornate Al Sahaba Mosque, lit up at night.
facts: Best in the evening

places.name: Ras Mohammed National Park
places.summary: The southern tip of Sinai, where reef walls drop hundreds of metres into the deep: Shark & Yolanda reef, the Anemone City pinnacle and huge shoals of fish. By boat for snorkelling or diving, or by car to the beaches and the mangroves.
facts: Full-day boat trip ~€35–60; park fee ~US$5
Also reachable by car/taxi: beaches with reef entry
places.caution: Sinai-only visa stamps don't cover Ras Mohammed. With a full Egyptian visa (as on this trip) it's fine.

places.name: Straits of Tiran reefs (boat)
places.summary: Four reefs in the middle of the straits (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon), with wrecks on top and big fish and currents. A classic Sharm dive and snorkel day.
facts: ~€35–60 with lunch
Currents: snorkellers should stay with the guide
places.caution: Boats stay out when the port is closed for wind.

places.name: Sharm el-Sheikh Airport (SSH)
places.summary: 15 min north of Naama Bay; EgyptAir flies to Cairo in 1 h, and many direct flights to Europe.

places.name: Dahab
places.summary: Laid-back former Bedouin village turned backpacker and dive town: a seafront promenade of cushioned cafés, shore dives right off the street (Lighthouse, Eel Garden) and the mountains behind.
facts: Cheap, friendly guesthouses and dive centres
Good base for Mount Sinai (2 h) and the Blue Hole (20 min)

places.name: Blue Hole & the Bells (Dahab)
places.summary: A deep sinkhole in the reef just off the shore, ringed with coral and full of fish: stunning snorkelling along the rim. Divers enter at the Bells and drift along the wall.
facts: Snorkel gear can be rented at the beach cafés
Entry fee ~US$5
places.caution: Famous for deaths of deep divers: stay within your training and never go through the arch.

places.name: Ras Abu Galum protected area
places.summary: A roadless Bedouin bay north of the Blue Hole, reached by a 1-hour coastal walk, camel or boat: reefs, empty beaches and simple huts for tea and fish.
facts: Start at the Blue Hole; take water and a sun hat

places.name: St Catherine (Bedouin guesthouses)
places.summary: A small mountain town at 1,600 m, base for Mount Sinai, the monastery and Bedouin-guided treks (Jebel Abbas Basha, the gardens of Wadi Itlah).
places.season: Cold at night in Nov–Dec (near 0 °C at the summit before dawn): bring warm layers, gloves and a hat.

places.name: Mount Sinai sunrise hike
places.note: Start ~02:00 from the monastery car park; sunrise at the summit; back down by ~08:30.
places.summary: Climb the 2,285 m mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments, by the camel path in the dark, then the last 750 steps to the summit to watch sunrise over the Sinai ranges. Come down by the 3,750 Steps of Repentance, straight to the monastery.
facts: ~3 h up; a Bedouin guide is required (arranged at the gate or by your guesthouse)
Camels can take you most of the way up
places.caution: Freezing before dawn in winter: rent a blanket at the top or bring a down jacket.

places.name: St Catherine's Monastery
places.summary: One of the oldest working Christian monasteries in the world (6th century, UNESCO), at the foot of Mount Sinai: the Burning Bush, an extraordinary icon collection and an ancient library.
facts: Short opening (mornings only); closed Fridays, Sundays and Orthodox holidays
Modest dress: knees and shoulders covered
Pairs perfectly with the descent from Mount Sinai

places.name: Coloured Canyon (Nuweiba)
places.summary: A narrow slot canyon with walls striped red, yellow and purple, walked in about an hour. Reached by 4×4 from Dahab or Nuweiba.
facts: Go with a jeep tour from Dahab (half day)

bookings.note: Or open-jaw: into Cairo, home from Sharm el-Sheikh or Hurghada.
US$25 single entry. visa2egypt.gov.eg, or at the bank counter in arrivals.
Book for the first Luxor morning so a wind cancellation can move to the next day.
Paid by card at each gate. Luxor Pass may be cheaper.
Snorkel or 2 dives; park fee extra.
Required; arranged at the gate or by the guesthouse.

checklist: Passport valid 6+ months after arrival, with 2 blank pages. Visa: e-visa beforehand or US$25 on arrival (cash, USD or EUR).
Arriving straight into Sharm? The free 'Sinai only' stamp covers the Aqaba coast only (not Ras Mohammed, not the rest of Egypt). Starting in Cairo, you need the full visa.
Check current travel advice: North Sinai and the Libyan border area are no-go; South Sinai resorts, the Red Sea coast and the Nile Valley are routinely visited.
Carry your passport (not a copy) on every road trip between cities: there are police checkpoints.
Travel between cities in daylight. Book flights, the ferry and sleeper trains ahead in high season (Nov–Feb).
A card that works abroad for site ticket offices (card only), and small cash notes for taxis, toilets and tips.
Install Uber and Careem; save your hotels' addresses in Arabic.
Drones are banned without a permit and are confiscated on arrival.
Shoulders and knees covered at mosques, churches and St Catherine's; a scarf for women in mosques.
Drink bottled water only; sunscreen, hat and 1–2 L water per person on temple days.
Travel insurance that covers diving if you plan to dive; bring your certification card.
Ramadan (around Feb–Mar 2027) shortens opening hours, if your dates move into it.
